problem: VLM-based object navigation agents either reason only over current observations (ignoring history and exploration progress) or reason at every step, which is expensive; existing dual-system designs use separate models and rigid heuristic switching.
motivation: Object navigation needs spatial reasoning, long-term memory and long-horizon planning, yet dense reasoning adds large latency (e.g. corridors need only reactive control). The paper wants a single VLM that reasons over memory and history but triggers reasoning only when needed.
key_idea: A single Qwen2.5-VL-7B agent with a slow (memory-based reasoning + panoramic scan) and a fast (reactive action) mode that self-switches via an 'obs' token, trained by a 3-stage curriculum ending with iterative rejection fine-tuning that teaches it to reason at stagnation points.
insight: Reasoning plus memory yields most of the SR gain (Stage 1→2: HM3D SR 39.8→72.9), while adaptive triggering via IRFT further raises SR (to 84.8) and efficiency (reasoning ratio ~3%, OVON-Unseen SOT 12.3→22.2). Ablations: removing memory keeps SR but collapses SPL (HM3D 13.9 vs 27.7); exploration trajectories vs shortest-path-only give +25.4 SR on HM3D; skipping Stage 1 costs 4.9 SR HM3D and 9.1 OVON.
method: Dual-process single VLM: slow system takes goal, 4-view panorama and long-term memory and outputs <think> reasoning plus an action; fast system decodes low-level actions from the latest frame with KV cache.
Long-term memory: serialized graph of landmark nodes (4-image panoramas) connected by action edges, pruned to at most 10 landmarks (start/end kept, others uniformly sampled).
Adaptive switching: model emits 'obs' token to trigger a panoramic scan, add a landmark and re-enter slow mode (forced at 30 fast steps).
Stage 1 spatial-action alignment: 500K A* trajectories from HM3D/MP3D/OVON train sets, multi-turn SFT of actions only.

Stage 2 reasoning-memory integration: exploration trajectories via top-2 scored waypoints, 16-step segments, hindsight reasoning synthesized by Qwen3-VL-235B-Thinking using future view as hidden guide, filtered by LLM, co-trained with VQA data.

Stage 3 IRFT: on-policy rollouts, slow system forced at stagnation points (revisit within 0.5m after 20 steps, or no progress over 20-35 steps); failed trajectories repaired by inserting obs at t* and appending an A* path with synthesized reasoning; 3 rounds.
SOT metric: success weighted by optimal time over actual time (robot execution time plus token-based inference latency).

setting.training_data: 500K A* trajectories (HM3D/MP3D/OVON train), 565K mixed samples in Stage 2 (synthetic reasoning from Qwen3-VL-235B plus VQA data), ~60K trajectories per IRFT round
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (640x480), panoramic 4x90° scan at obs; no depth
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MoveAhead 0.25m, Rotate Left/Right 30°, obs, end (plus reasoning text)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT positions used only for training data generation)

numbers.extra: 3 IRFT turns; trained on HM3D/MP3D/OVON train data

numbers_note: SOT values for stages appear mostly in figures; Appendix Table reports HM3D IRFT Turn3 SR 84.3, SOT 24.0, OVON-Unseen SOT 20.3, reasoning ratio 3.0%/3.5% (slightly different from Table 1).
results: Hydra-Nav-IRFT reaches SR 84.8 on HM3D (vs Uni-Navid 73.7), 64.0 on MP3D (vs CogNav 46.6) and 66.3 on OVON Val-Unseen (vs NavFoM 45.2), with SPL best on all splits. It reasons in only ~3% of steps and attains higher SOT than VLMnav, Nav-R2 and WMNav.
limitations: Evaluated only in Habitat; no other simulators or realistic benchmarks
Real-world deployment is only qualitative (a few episodes, no numbers)
SOT depends on assumed per-token latency and action time constants
